 Announcements
 By Ashish Agarwal 
 Nov 06, 2026
 Central Bank of India (NSE:CENTRALBK): What Happened at Its Analyst Meet With Motilal Oswal?
 CENTRALBK
 Source: Krish Capital Pty Ltd
 You are reading a free article with opinions that may differ from the recommendation given by Kalkine in its paid research reports. Become a Kalkine member today to get access to our research reports, in-depth technical and fundamental research. Learn More 
 Central Bank of India (NSE:CENTRALBK) disclosed on 6 November 2026, pursuant to Regulation 30 of the SEBI Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements Regulations 2015, that its management participated in a virtual one-on-one analyst and investor meeting with Motilal Oswal on the same date.
 Key Highlights
 The bank's management held a virtual one-on-one meeting with Motilal Oswal on 6 November 2026, as disclosed under SEBI Regulation 30.
 The filing explicitly states that only information already available in the public domain was discussed during the meeting.
 The disclosure was submitted by Chandrakant Bhagwat, Company Secretary and Compliance Officer, to both NSE and BSE simultaneously.
 The bank's registered communication for this filing originates from its Central Office at Chander Mukhi, Nariman Point, Mumbai.
 About the Company
 Central Bank of India (NSE:CENTRALBK) is a public sector bank headquartered at Chander Mukhi, Nariman Point, Mumbai. Established in 1911, it offers a wide range of banking and financial services including retail deposits, corporate lending, agricultural credit, MSME financing, and treasury operations across an extensive branch network spanning urban, semi-urban, and rural India. The bank is listed on both NSE and BSE under scrip codes CENTRALBK and 532885 respectively, and falls within the Banking and Financial Services sector.
 Announcement in Detail
 Pursuant to Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, Central Bank of India informed the exchanges that its management participated in an analyst and investor meet on 6 November 2026. The meeting was held in a virtual format and was structured as a one-on-one interaction with Motilal Oswal, a leading domestic brokerage and financial services firm. The filing, bearing reference CO:IRD:2026:27:205, was submitted on the same date as the meeting.
 The bank stated clearly in the disclosure that only information available in the public domain was discussed during the course of the meeting. No new material non-public information was shared with the participants. The filing was addressed to the Listing Departments of both the National Stock Exchange of India Limited and BSE Limited, ensuring simultaneous and symmetric disclosure to all market participants in keeping with SEBI's fair disclosure requirements.
 Impact on Investors
 Investors will note that this filing carries no new financial disclosures, forward guidance, or operational updates beyond what the bank has already placed on record through its regular exchange filings. The meeting with Motilal Oswal was confined to publicly available information, as explicitly confirmed in the announcement, which limits any information asymmetry concern for retail shareholders.
 Shareholders will observe that the bank's compliance with Regulation 30 disclosure norms reflects adherence to SEBI's fair disclosure framework. The filing shows no material change in the bank's stated position, capital structure, or strategic direction as a result of this interaction. No dilution, pledge activity, or covenant-related event has been disclosed in connection with this meeting.
 Sector / Market Context
 Indian public sector banks have faced renewed investor scrutiny in recent years following improvements in asset quality metrics across the sector, with gross non-performing asset ratios for scheduled commercial banks declining as reported in successive Reserve Bank of India Financial Stability Reports. Analyst and investor engagement meetings have become a standard part of the investor relations calendar for listed public sector banks, supporting price discovery and improving institutional coverage. SEBI's Regulation 30 framework mandates timely disclosure of such interactions to maintain market integrity and equal access to information across all categories of investors.
